title: March PDO gave no clear added winter Nino 3.4 forecast skill in 1981-2024
abstract: We tested whether March Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) adds information about November-January Nino 3.4 after current and prior December Nino 3.4 and a year term are known. Each of 44 forecasts in 1981-2024 used earlier years only. Adding PDO raised mean squared error by 2.59%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -7.96% to +2.30%. The primary baseline also had more error than the training mean. June, 30-year fit, no-trend and tropical spatial-control checks all had negative point gains. This is a negative forecast benchmark, not a test that excludes a physical North Pacific effect on ENSO. Short dependent records, revised shared surface data, weak baseline skill and model form limit inference. The package includes original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes, an independent numerical audit and reproduction steps. External source and annual record tables stay outside the signed package.

display.caption: Adding PDO raised point forecast error in all five planned models. Lines show conditional paired five-year block intervals.

citations.reason: Published reverse-direction benchmark and shared data sources. Data overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
